title: KCET 2019 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q:
Among the following, the main reactions occurring in blast furnace during extraction of iron from haematite are
i. Fe$_2$O$_3$ + 3CO $\longrightarrow$ 2Fe + 3CO$_2$
ii. FeO + SiO$_2$ $\longrightarrow$ FeSiO$_3$
iii. Fe$_2$O$_3$ + 3C $\longrightarrow$ 2Fe + 3CO
iv. CaO + SiO$_2$ $\longrightarrow$ CaSiO$_3$
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: In the blast furnace, Fe2O3 is reduced by CO (reaction i) and CaO combines with SiO2 gangue to form slag CaSiO3 (reaction iv); these are the two main reactions, so option D is correct.

questions.q: Which of the following pair contains 2 lone pairs of electrons on the central atom?
questions.explanation: In I3+ the central I atom has 2 lone pairs (bent shape) and in H2O the central O atom also has 2 lone pairs, so option A is correct.

questions.q: Which of the following statement is correct?
options: Cl$_2$ oxidises H$_2$O to O$_2$ but F$_2$ does not.
F$_2$ oxidises H$_2$O to O$_2$ but Cl$_2$ does not.
Cl$_2$ is a stronger oxidizing agent than F$_2$.
Fluoride is a good oxidising agent.
questions.explanation: F2 has a much higher reduction potential than Cl2 and vigorously oxidises water to O2 (with HF formation), while Cl2 only partially reacts with water to form HOCl and HCl.

questions.q: 0.1 mole of XeF$_6$ is treated with 1.8 g of water. The product obtained is
questions.explanation: 1.8 g water = 0.1 mol, which reacts with XeF6 in 1:1 ratio (partial hydrolysis) to give XeOF4 + 2HF; complete hydrolysis to XeO3 needs 3 mol water per mole XeF6.

questions.q: In the reaction of gold with aquaregia, oxidation state of Nitrogen changes from
questions.explanation: In aqua regia, HNO3 (N in +5 state) is reduced to NO (N in +2 state); the NO reacts further with Cl- to release nascent chlorine that dissolves gold.

questions.q: The vitamin that helps in clotting of blood is
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of clotting factors (prothrombin) in blood.

questions.q: The polymer containing five methylene groups in its repeating unit is
questions.explanation: Nylon 6 is made from caprolactam, -[NH-(CH2)5-CO]-, whose repeat unit contains five methylene (CH2) groups.

questions.q: Cis-1, 4-polyisoprene is called
questions.explanation: Natural rubber is the cis-1,4-polymer of isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene).

questions.q: Which cleansing agent gets precipitated in hard water?
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Sodium stearate is a soap; its Ca2+/Mg2+ salts formed with hard water ions are insoluble and precipitate out, unlike synthetic detergents.

questions.q: Anti-histamine among the following is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Bromopheneramine is an antihistamine used to treat allergies; amoxycillin is an antibiotic, morphine an analgesic, and chloroxylenol an antiseptic.

questions.q: The mass of AgCl precipitated when a solution containing 11.70 g of NaCl is added to a solution containing 3.4 g of AgNO$_3$ is [Atomic mass of Ag = 108, Atomic mass of Na = 23]
questions.explanation: Moles NaCl = 11.70/58.5 = 0.2; moles AgNO3 = 3.4/170 = 0.02 (limiting reagent); moles AgCl formed = 0.02, mass = 0.02 $\times$ 143.5 = 2.87 g.

questions.q: Two particles A and B are in motion. If the wavelength associated with 'A' is 33.33 nm, the wavelength associated with 'B' whose momentum is $\dfrac{1}{3}$rd of 'A' is
questions.explanation: Since $\lambda = h/p$, if $p_B = p_A/3$ then $\lambda_B = 3\lambda_A = 3 \times 33.33$ nm $\approx 1.0\times10^{-7}$ m.

questions.q: The first ionization enthalpy of the following elements are in the order:
questions.explanation: Ionization enthalpy increases across a period and decreases down a group; among C, N, Si, P the correct increasing order is Si < P < C < N (N has extra stability from a half-filled 2p subshell).

questions.q: Solubility of AgCl is least in
questions.explanation: AlCl3 provides the highest concentration of common Cl- ion (0.3 M), so by the common-ion effect it suppresses the solubility of AgCl the most.

questions.q: Which of the following equations does NOT represent Charles's law for a given mass of gas at constant pressure?
questions.explanation: Charles's law V/T = K gives, on taking logs, log V = log K + log T (option C), and differentiating gives d(ln V)/dT = 1/T (option D); option B (log K = log V + log T) would imply K = VT, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Which is the most suitable reagent for the following conversion?
CH$_3$-CH=CH-CH$_2$-CO-CH$_3$ $\longrightarrow$ CH$_3$-CH=CH-CH$_2$-COOH
questions.explanation: I2/NaOH brings about the haloform reaction, converting the methyl ketone to a carboxylic acid (losing one carbon as CHI3) without touching the isolated C=C double bond.

questions.q: Which of the following is least soluble in water at 298 K?
questions.explanation: Aniline's large hydrophobic phenyl ring makes it far less water soluble than the small aliphatic methylamines.

questions.q: If Aniline is treated with 1:1 mixture of con. HNO$_3$ and con. H$_2$SO$_4$, p-nitroaniline and m-nitroaniline are formed nearly in equal amounts. This is due to
options: m and p directing property of -NH$_2$ group
protonation of -NH$_2$ which causes deactivation of benzene ring
isomerization of some p-nitroaniline into m-nitroaniline
questions.explanation: In the strongly acidic medium, -NH2 is protonated to -NH3+, which is a deactivating, meta-directing group, so a significant fraction of meta product forms alongside the para product from unprotonated aniline.

questions.q: In nucleic acids, the nucleotides are joined together by
questions.explanation: Successive nucleotides in DNA/RNA are linked through 3'-5' phosphodiester bonds.

questions.q: Which of the following is generally water insoluble?
questions.explanation: Fibrous proteins (e.g. keratin, collagen) have extended structures held by strong intermolecular H-bonding and are water insoluble, unlike globular proteins, amylose, vitamin C or glycine.

questions.q:
Match the following acids with their pKa values:
a. Phenol   i. 16
b. p-Nitrophenol   ii. 0.78
c. Ethanol   iii. 10
d. Picric acid   iv. 7.1
questions.explanation: Phenol (pKa$\approx$10), p-nitrophenol (pKa$\approx$7.1, more acidic due to -NO2), ethanol (pKa$\approx$16, weakly acidic), picric acid (pKa$\approx$0.78, strongly acidic) — matching a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.q: Which of the following can be used to test the acidic nature of ethanol?
questions.explanation: Ethanol is too weak an acid to react with litmus or the carbonates/bicarbonates, but it reacts with reactive sodium metal to liberate H2 gas, confirming its (weak) acidic nature.

questions.q: [Structure: HOCH$_2$-CH=CH-CHO is converted by three different reagents A, B, C respectively into (i) HOCH$_2$-CH=CH-CH$_2$OH (via A), (ii) OHC-CH=CH-CHO (via B), and (iii) HOCH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$OH, the saturated diol, via C.] The reagents A, B and C respectively are
questions.explanation: NaBH4 selectively reduces the aldehyde to a primary alcohol without touching the alkene (A), PCC mildly oxidises the primary alcohol to an aldehyde, again leaving the alkene untouched (B), and H2/Pd catalytic hydrogenation reduces both the C=C double bond and the aldehyde, giving the saturated diol HOCH2CH2CH2CH2OH (C); matching option B.

questions.q: Propanoic acid undergoes HVZ reaction to give chloropropanoic acid. The product obtained is
questions.explanation: The electron-withdrawing Cl substituent introduced alpha to the carboxyl group by the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction stabilises the carboxylate anion inductively, making chloropropanoic acid a stronger acid than propanoic acid.

questions.q:
P $\xrightarrow{H_2/Pd-BaSO_4}$ Q $\xrightarrow[(ii)\ dil.\ HCl]{(i)\ con.\ NaOH}$ R + S.
R and S form benzyl benzoate when treated with each other. Hence P is
questions.explanation: Rosenmund reduction (H2/Pd-BaSO4) of benzoyl chloride (P) gives benzaldehyde (Q), which undergoes Cannizzaro reaction with conc. NaOH to give benzyl alcohol (R) and sodium benzoate (giving benzoic acid, S, after acidification); R and S then esterify to form benzyl benzoate.

questions.q: The elements in which electrons are progressively filled in 4f orbital are called
questions.explanation: Lanthanoids (atomic numbers 58-71) have electrons progressively filling the 4f orbitals.

questions.q: Incorrect statement with reference to Ce (Z = 58)
options: Atomic size of Ce is more than that of Lu.
Ce in +3 oxidation state is more stable than in +4.
Ce shows common oxidation states of +3 and +4.
questions.explanation: Ce4+ is actually a good oxidising agent (it readily gets reduced to the more stable Ce3+), so the statement that it is a reducing agent is incorrect.

questions.q: A mixture of NaCl and K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ is heated with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$; deep red vapours are formed. Which of the following statement is false?
options: The vapours give a yellow solution with NaOH.
The vapours contain CrO$_2$Cl$_2$ and Cl$_2$.
The vapours when passed into lead acetate in acetic acid gives a yellow precipitate.
questions.explanation: The chromyl chloride test produces pure CrO2Cl2 vapours, not a mixture with free Cl2; statement B is therefore false, while A, C and D correctly describe the test.

questions.q: Which of the following statement is wrong?
options: In highest oxidation states, the transition metals show acidic character.
Metals in highest oxidation states are more stable in oxides than in fluorides.
Mn$^{3+}$ and Co$^{3+}$ are oxidizing agents in aqueous solution.
All elements of 3d series exhibit variable oxidation states.
questions.explanation: Not all 3d elements show variable oxidation states — e.g. Sc shows only +3 and Zn shows only +2 — so statement D is wrong.

questions.q: Which among the following is the strongest ligand?
questions.explanation: In the spectrochemical series, CO produces the largest crystal field splitting and is considered the strongest ligand among these choices.

questions.q: Which of the following possess net dipole moment?
questions.explanation: SO2 has a bent (V-shaped) geometry so its bond dipoles do not cancel, giving it a net dipole moment; BeCl2, BF3 and CO2 are symmetric and non-polar.

questions.q: The number of $\pi$-bonds and $\sigma$-bonds present in naphthalene are respectively
questions.explanation: Naphthalene (C10H8) has 5 C=C double bonds (5 pi bonds) and 19 sigma bonds (11 C-C + 8 C-H).

questions.q: The reaction in which $\Delta H > \Delta U$ is
questions.explanation: $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$, so $\Delta H > \Delta U$ requires $\Delta n_g > 0$; only the decomposition of CaCO3(s) increases moles of gas (0 to 1), giving $\Delta n_g = +1$.

questions.q: The number of moles of electron required to reduce 0.2 mole of Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$ to Cr$^{3+}$
questions.explanation: Each Cr goes from +6 to +3 (gain of 3 e- per Cr, 6 e- per Cr2O7^2- ion since it has 2 Cr atoms); for 0.2 mol Cr2O7^2-, electrons required = 0.2 $\times$ 6 = 1.2 mol.

questions.q: In the reaction B(OH)$_3$ + 2H$_2$O $\longrightarrow$ [B(OH)$_4$]$^-$ + H$_3$O$^+$, B(OH)$_3$ functions as
questions.explanation: Boric acid does not ionise to release a proton itself; instead the boron atom (electron-deficient) accepts a lone pair (as OH-) from a water molecule, so it acts as a Lewis acid.

questions.q: Addition of excess of AgNO$_3$ to an aqueous solution of 1 mole of PdCl$_2$.4NH$_3$ gives 2 moles of AgCl. The conductivity of this solution corresponds to
questions.explanation: Since 2 mol of ionisable Cl- are precipitated per mole of complex, the compound must be [Pd(NH3)4]Cl2, which ionises as 1 cation : 2 anions, i.e. a 1:2 electrolyte.

questions.q: The formula of penta aquanitrato chromium (III) nitrate is
questions.explanation: Penta aqua nitrato chromium(III) has the coordination sphere [Cr(H2O)5(NO3)]2+, balanced by two nitrate counter ions: [Cr(H2O)5NO3](NO3)2.

questions.q: Which of the following halide undergoes hydrolysis on warming with water/aqueous NaOH?
options: 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene (picryl chloride, Cl with NO$_2$ at 2,4,6 positions)
questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing -NO2 groups ortho/para to the C-Cl bond activate the ring for nucleophilic aromatic substitution; with three -NO2 groups (2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene) hydrolysis occurs most readily, even on warming with water.

questions.q: The compound having longest C-Cl bond is
questions.explanation: In chlorobenzene, p-nitrochlorobenzene and vinyl chloride, the C-Cl bond has partial double-bond character from conjugation with the pi system, shortening it; in 3-chlorocyclohexene the Cl is on an sp3 carbon with no such conjugation, so its C-Cl bond is the longest.

questions.q: The alkyl halides required to prepare 2-methylpentane, (CH$_3$)$_2$CHCH$_2$CH$_2$CH$_3$, by Wurtz reaction are
questions.explanation: Cross Wurtz coupling of isopropyl chloride, (CH3)2CHCl, with n-propyl chloride, CH3CH2CH2Cl, joins the two fragments to give (CH3)2CH-CH2CH2CH3, i.e. 2-methylpentane.

questions.q: The metal nitrate that liberates NO$_2$ on heating is
questions.explanation: Like the alkaline earth metal nitrates, LiNO3 decomposes on heating to give the oxide, NO2 and O2, because of Li+'s small size (diagonal relationship with Mg); heavier alkali metal nitrates (Na, K, Rb) decompose only to the nitrite and O2.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding the usage of hydrogen as a fuel?
options: The combustible energy of hydrogen can be directly converted to electrical energy in a fuel cell.
Hydrogen gas can be easily liquefied and stored.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen has a very low boiling point and is actually difficult and energy-intensive to liquefy and store, so statement D is not true.

questions.q: Resonance effect is not observed in
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: In CH2=CH-CH2-NH2 the lone pair on nitrogen is separated from the double bond by an sp3 CH2 group, so it cannot conjugate with the pi system and no resonance occurs.

questions.q: 2-butyne is reduced to trans-but-2-ene using
questions.explanation: Dissolving-metal reduction with sodium in liquid ammonia reduces alkynes to the trans (E) alkene.

questions.q: Eutrophication causes
questions.explanation: Eutrophication (excess nutrients causing algal overgrowth and decay) leads to depletion of dissolved oxygen in the water body.

questions.q: Which is a wrong statement?
options: Rate constant k = Arrhenius constant A, if Ea = 0
ln k vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ plot is a straight line.
e$^{-Ea/RT}$ gives the fraction of reactant molecules that are activated at the given temp
presence of catalyst will not alter the value of Ea
questions.explanation: A catalyst works precisely by lowering the activation energy Ea, so the statement that a catalyst does not alter Ea is wrong.

questions.q: 1 L of 2 M CH$_3$COOH is mixed with 1 L of 3M C$_2$H$_5$OH to form an ester. The rate of the reaction with respect to the initial rate when each solution is diluted with an equal volume of water will be
questions.explanation: Esterification rate $\propto$ [acid][alcohol]; diluting each solution with an equal volume of water halves both concentrations, so the new rate is $(1/2)\times(1/2)=1/4=0.25$ times the initial rate.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of homogeneous catalysis?
options: oxidation of NH$_3$ in Ostwald's process
oxidation of SO$_2$ in lead chamber process
oxidation of SO$_2$ in contact process
manufacture of NH$_3$ by Haber's process
questions.explanation: In the lead chamber process, NO gas catalyses the oxidation of SO2 while remaining in the same (gas) phase as the reactants, making it homogeneous catalysis; the other three use solid catalysts with gaseous reactants (heterogeneous).

questions.q: Critical Micelle concentration for a soap solution is $1.5\times10^{-4}$ mol L$^{-1}$. Micelle formation is possible only when the concentration of soap solution in mol L$^{-1}$ is
questions.explanation: Micelles form only above the CMC ($1.5\times10^{-4}$ mol L$^{-1}$); only $2.0\times10^{-3}$ mol L$^{-1}$ exceeds this value.

questions.q: Oxidation state of copper is +1 in
questions.explanation: In cuprite (Cu2O), copper is in the +1 state; KEA also accepted chalcopyrite (CuFeS2), which is conventionally assigned Cu+1, Fe3+, S2-, giving copper a +1 state there too. Malachite and azurite are Cu(II) basic carbonates.

questions.q: Relative lowering of vapour pressure of a dilute solution of glucose dissolved in 1 kg of water is 0.002. The molality of the solution is
questions.explanation: For a dilute solution, relative lowering of vapour pressure $\approx x_{solute} = n_{solute}/n_{solvent}$; with $n_{solvent}=1000/18=55.5$ mol, $n_{solute}=0.002\times55.5\approx0.111$ mol, giving molality $\approx0.111$ mol/kg.

questions.q: One litre solution of MgCl$_2$ is electrolyzed completely by passing a current of 1A for 16 min 5 sec. The original concentration of MgCl$_2$ solution was (Atomic mass of Mg = 24)
questions.explanation: Charge passed = 1A $\times$ 965 s = 965 C, i.e. 965/96500 = 0.01 mol electrons; since Mg2+ + 2e- $\rightarrow$ Mg, moles Mg (=moles MgCl2) completely deposited = 0.01/2 = 0.005 mol in 1 L, giving $5\times10^{-3}$ M.

questions.q: An aqueous solution of CuSO$_4$ is subjected to electrolysis using inert electrodes. The pH of the solution will
options: increase or decrease depending on the strength of the current.
questions.explanation: At the anode, water is oxidised to O2 releasing H+ ions (SO4^2- is not oxidised preferentially), while Cu2+ is reduced at the cathode; the accumulation of H+ makes the solution more acidic, so pH decreases.

questions.q: Given: E$^\circ_{Mn^{+7}/Mn^{+2}}$ = 1.5 V and E$^\circ_{Mn^{+4}/Mn^{+2}}$ = 1.2 V, then E$^\circ_{Mn^{+7}/Mn^{+4}}$ is
questions.explanation: Using $\Delta G$ additivity: $5(1.5) = 2(1.2) + 3E^\circ_{Mn^{+7}/Mn^{+4}}$, so $7.5-2.4=3E^\circ$, giving $E^\circ=1.7$ V.

questions.q: The plot of t$_{1/2}$ v/s [R]$_0$ for a reaction is a straight-line parallel to x-axis. The unit for the rate constant of this reaction is
questions.explanation: t1/2 independent of initial concentration ([R]0) is the hallmark of a first-order reaction, whose rate constant has units of s$^{-1}$.

questions.q: Which of the following is a network crystalline solid?
questions.explanation: AlN has a diamond-like covalent network structure, unlike molecular solids I2 and ice or the ionic solid NaCl.

questions.q: The number of atoms in 2.4 g of body centred cubic crystal with edge length 200 pm is (density = 10 g cm$^{-3}$, N$_A$ = $6\times10^{23}$ atoms/mol)
questions.explanation: Using $\rho = ZM/(N_A a^3)$ with Z=2, $a=2\times10^{-8}$ cm: $M = 10\times6\times10^{23}\times(2\times10^{-8})^3/2 = 24$ g/mol; moles of atoms in 2.4 g $= 2.4/24=0.1$, giving $0.1\times6\times10^{23}=6\times10^{22}$ atoms.

questions.q: 1 mole of NaCl is doped with $10^{-5}$ mole of SrCl$_2$. The number of cationic vacancies in the crystal lattice will be
questions.explanation: Each Sr2+ ion occupies one Na+ site but supplies the charge of two Na+ ions, so it creates exactly one cation vacancy; $10^{-5}$ mol Sr2+ therefore creates $10^{-5}\times6.022\times10^{23}=6.022\times10^{18}$ vacancies.

questions.q: A non-volatile solute 'A' tetramerises in water to the extent of 80%. 2.5 g of 'A' in 100 g of water lowers the freezing point by 0.3 $^\circ$C. The molar mass of A in g mol$^{-1}$ is (K$_f$ for water = 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: Association into tetramers with 80% association gives van't Hoff factor $i=1-\alpha+\alpha/4=1-0.8+0.2=0.4$; molality $m=(2.5\times1000)/(M\times100)=25/M$; $\Delta T_f=iK_fm \Rightarrow 0.3=0.4\times1.86\times(25/M) \Rightarrow M=62$ g/mol.

questions.q: Solution 'A' contains acetone dissolved in chloroform and solution 'B' contains acetone dissolved in carbon disulphide. The type of deviations from Raoult's law shown by solutions A and B, respectively are
questions.explanation: Acetone-chloroform interactions (H-bonding) are stronger than the pure component interactions, causing negative deviation (solution A), while acetone-CS2 interactions are weaker, causing positive deviation (solution B).
